source.title: Not All Clients Are Equal: Personalized Federated Learning on Heterogeneous Multi-Modal Clients
source.authors: Minhyuk Seo; Taeheon Kim; Hankook Lee; Jonghyun Choi; T. Tuytelaars

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representation similarity with CKA across model layers, a different measure from the claim’s original approach, and uses the results to assess layer correspondence.
record.gate_note: The CKA layer-alignment analyses in Figures 4 and 12–13 bear on representational alignment. The federated-learning accuracy results, Co-LoRA task-performance results, and other benchmark results do not measure the claim’s convergence behavior and are excluded. The text does not test whether alignment increases with model scale or capability, or compare similarity measures or inputs.
record.test_reason: This is a federated-learning methods paper (FedMosaic, Co-LoRA, RELA). Its CKA heat maps (Fig. 4, 12, 13) are a design check to decide which layers to aggregate. They show that layers at similar relative depth are most similar across models. They do not measure whether alignment grows with scale or capability (V1), vision-language pairing (V2), seeds (V3), mapping or stitching loss (V4), shared features (V5), or metric dependence (V6/V7). No CKA values are given, and there is no trend across model sizes. The CCA/L2 alignment of LoRA matrices is judged only by downstream task accuracy (Tab. 32), not by representation-mapping loss. The CKA observation is a related but different construct (layer-depth correspondence), so it belongs under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the CKA side analysis. The paper's main conclusion is that FedMosaic outperforms PFL baselines and local SFT under data and model heterogeneity. RELA (relevance-guided aggregation) and Co-LoRA (dimension-invariant shared modules) drive this, evaluated on the new DRAKE benchmark. The relative-depth CKA observation is used only to justify block-wise Co-LoRA aggregation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses layerwise CKA to identify relative-depth correspondences across multimodal model families; it does not reproduce a convergence-with-scale measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: CKA between hidden states of different-size and different-family MLLMs is highest for layers at similar relative depth. The pattern holds within Llama-3, within Qwen-2.5, and between InternVL and LLaVA. It is weaker but near-linear between Llama and Qwen. Figure-only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layerwise representational correspondence between models of different depth follows relative depth, more strongly within a model family than across families.

record.problems: The representation-alignment findings are described qualitatively from CKA figures, without numerical similarity values or uncertainty estimates. The analysis does not test an increase in alignment with scale or capability, and does not directly measure mapping or stitching loss.
record.rows_left_out: Federated-learning task accuracy and adaptation results are not representation-similarity measurements and were excluded. Other reported ablations concern task performance, privacy, or computational cost, not the claim’s convergence behavior.

untested.parts: No measurement of alignment versus model size or capability. The CKA maps are not compared across scales quantitatively.
No separate vision and language models compared on paired image-caption data.
There is no measure of how much is lost when mapping or stitching one model's representations onto another's. The CCA alignment of LoRA B matrices is evaluated only through federated task accuracy.
No feature, neuron or circuit comparison.
Only CKA on one input set. No comparison of metrics or inputs.
No analysis of how far alignment falls short of complete, whether it plateaus, or what causes it.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'tests' and supports/limits_scope labels are removed. Relative-depth CKA similarity is not evidence that representations map onto each other with little loss. No CKA numbers, controls or scale trend are reported. Tab. 32 (A and B alignment vs random) shows small accuracy differences only, so it is not a representation measure.

versions.untested_parts: No test of whether alignment increases with model size or capability, or across independently trained models with differing objectives and data.
No separate vision and language models evaluated on paired images and captions, and no test of alignment as both improve.
No comparison of models trained from different initializations of the same architecture for shared features or subspaces.
The study measures layerwise CKA and relative-depth correspondence, but does not directly test whether representations can be mapped or stitched with little loss.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
No comparison across similarity metrics, metric settings, or input distributions.
No test of whether shared data or objectives explain alignment, or whether alignment is incomplete or plateaus.

rows.subject: Llama-3 family (1B, 3B, 8B)
rows.operation_detail: Measured layerwise representation similarity with CKA across model scales.
rows.value: figure only; text says layers at similar relative depths exhibit strong alignment
rows.note: The authors describe the strongest alignment as occurring between layers at similar relative depths. No numerical CKA values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Layerwise relative-depth CKA correspondence within Llama-3 (1B/3B/8B). It is not a mapping-loss measure (V4) and shows no trend with scale (V1). The values are figure-only, with no numbers or baseline.

rows.subject: Qwen-2.5 family (0.5B, 1.5B, 3B)
rows.operation_detail: Measured layerwise representation similarity with CKA across model scales.
rows.value: figure only; text says layers at similar relative depths exhibit strong alignment
rows.note: The text reports the same relative-depth alignment pattern for Qwen-2.5 models. No numerical CKA values are stated.
rows.check: The same relative-depth CKA pattern within Qwen-2.5 (0.5B/1.5B/3B). It does not measure V4 interchangeability or any scale trend. Figure-only.

rows.subject: Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 mixed models
rows.operation_detail: Measured layerwise representation similarity with CKA across model families.
rows.value: figure only; text says near-linear alignment occurs across families but is weaker than within-family alignment
rows.note: The authors report relative-depth alignment across families, while explicitly describing it as weaker than within-family alignment. No numerical CKA values are stated.
rows.check: Cross-family Llama vs Qwen CKA is described as near-linear but weaker than within-family. 'Weaker' refers to diagonal linearity, not to mapping loss, so this is not a V4 partial result. Figure-only.

rows.subject: InternVL with InternLM base LLM and LLaVA with Llama base LLM
rows.operation_detail: Measured layerwise representation similarity with CKA across models.
rows.value: figure only; text says layers with relative depth align most strongly
rows.note: The authors say the layer-correlation analysis shows the same relative-depth trend. No numerical CKA values are stated.
rows.check: InternVL/InternLM vs LLaVA/Llama relative-depth CKA trend. Model sizes are not stated. It is not a test of any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Within the tested Llama-3 and Qwen-2.5 families, and for the InternVL/InternLM versus LLaVA/Llama comparison
reader_labels.reason: CKA is described as showing strong or strongest alignment at similar relative depths, supporting layerwise correspondence in these tested comparisons (r1, r2, r4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Relative-depth alignment is reported across families, but the authors say it is weaker than within-family alignment (r3).
